title: Compareboard: unified rollout comparison dashboard for canary, A/B, and shadow cohorts
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a Compareboard view in the Redwood Console that lets operators compare live rollout cohorts (canary, A/B, shadow) across per-route metrics, latency & error traces, token-level cost, and distributional diffs for model outputs. The goal is to make regression detection and rollback decisions faster by surfacing ordered diffs, cohort-level metric overlays, and correlated trace samples. This ticket covers the PM scope: product requirements, acceptance criteria, prioritized UX flows, and coordination with ENG + Design to implement backend signals and frontend visualizations.
acceptance_criteria: Console has a Compareboard route accessible from a rollout detail page
Users can select up to 3 cohorts (baseline, canary, shadow) and overlay per-route metrics: p50/p95 latency, error rate, request throughput, token cost
Compareboard shows top-ranked diff signals (statistical deltas) with confidence and an explanation for why each signal is flagged
Operators can open 1-click trace samples for requests that contributed most to each signal and view the matching model response pairs side-by-side
Ability to filter diffs by user segment (country, workspace tier, route tag) and time window
Auto-rollback policy can be linked from Compareboard; PM flow documents required inputs for SRE/Eng to enforce
Performance: Compareboard loads summary overlays in <2s for 1M-sample window and individual traces in <1.5s in staging
Docs and a walk-through checklist are published in Confluence and linked from the rollout UI

2026-02-18 - Luca: Met with Eng (routing, metrics infra) and Design. ENG pointed out we need a compact aggregation pipeline for cohort-level token histograms; adding ENG-2189 as dependency.

2026-02-22 - Mei Chen (Design): Shared early mockups that emphasize a vertical diff list with sparklines and a side-by-side sample viewer. Design asked for clear affordance for linking auto-rollback policies.

2026-02-28 - Eng (Sofia): Feasibility: we can compute cohort deltas using existing metrics and a small add-on job that calculates deltas per-route hourly. For real-time detection (sub-minute), we'll need a streaming aggregator; proposed incremental rollout (hourly -> 5m -> real-time)

2026-03-03 - Asha: Prioritized signals for MVP: error rate delta, p95 latency delta, token cost drift, and semantic output divergence (BLEU-like metric for structured responses). Added task to define semantic metrics (ENG-2044).
2026-03-05 - Luca: Updated acceptance criteria with performance targets. Planned sync with SRE on alerting thresholds and runbook next week.
steps: Finalize PRD and get Design approval (blocked until semantic diff metric proposal is accepted)
Engineering to implement cohort-aggregation API and delta scorer (ENG-2189 / ENG-2044)
Design to deliver high-fidelity mockups and accessibility review
Frontend to implement Compareboard UI and integrate trace viewer
Integration testing with Dedicated and Private deployments to validate metric availability
Publish docs, run internal dogfood rollout, and collect operator feedback
Iterate on flagged signals; add auto-rollback policy wiring and safety checks
notes: Trade-offs discussed: showing too many diffs will overwhelm operators; we will surface top 5 signals by default with an expand control
Privacy: sample traces used for side-by-side comparison must be scrubbed for PII; coordinate with Privacy team to define scrubbing rules
We deliberately defer full time-series anomaly detection to a follow-up because it adds ML work; MVP uses statistically significant deltas with bootstrapped confidence intervals
Rollouts with shadow-only traffic: Compareboard will prioritize distribution diffs and per-token cost comparisons because latency/error signals are not meaningful
